sources.S2: INSEE, Panorama de l'appareil productif en 2023 — https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/8679855
sources.S3: INSEE, Ratios des secteurs marchands par activité en 2023 (Ésane) — https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/2015421
sources.S4: INSEE, Salaires dans le secteur privé, édition 2026 — https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/8733089
sources.S6: Acemoglu, Lelarge & Restrepo (2020), Competing with Robots: Firm-Level Evidence from France — https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257%2Fpandp.20201003

rgdu.note: Coefficient rounded to 4 decimals and capped at Tmin + Tdelta; zero from 3 reference SMIC. The reference SMIC stays at its 1 January 2026 value.

smic_current.source: arrêté of 22 May 2026: 12.31 € an hour from 1 June 2026
smic_current.note: Legal floor for gross wages only; never enters the RGDU formula.

contributions.source: URSSAF 2026 employer rates; S1 for the 0.49 % cap on the eligible AT/MP part
contributions.note: Full-time private-sector posts only. The reduced health and family rates no longer exist in 2026. Eligible rates below the ceiling sum to Tmin + Tdelta.

contributions.other_levies.source: training, apprenticeship tax, PEEC and transport levy; orders of magnitude by size
contributions.other_levies.note: Not eligible to the RGDU; shifts the level of labor costs, not the reform.

bands.source: target: S4, once gross (not net) distributions are at hand
bands.note: Representative gross wage of each band, in reference SMIC. S4 publishes net amounts, which are not converted here.

population.source: convention of the spec: 4 markets × 3 sizes × 10 replications
population.note: An experimental sample, uniform over the 12 cells: not representative of France. Results are read by market × size.

markets.va_rate.note: 'Industrie' stands in for manufacturing; the two perimeters are close but not identical.

markets.structure.source: no source; structural assumptions to sweep
markets.structure.note: Routine share of work, automatable share θ, band mix by task, AT/MP rate.

sizes.headcount.source: convention; the 50+ class is stylized at 50 to 250 posts
sizes.headcount.note: Large firms here are not national groups.

sizes.margins_cash.source: target: S2 (quartiles of EBE/VA and of cash by size); market shift from S3 once checked
sizes.margins_cash.note: Crossing size and market is itself an assumption, for want of a joint table. Margin and cash are drawn through a Gaussian copula.

costs.fixed_share_ci.note: Share of intermediate consumption that does not move with output (rent, overheads).

demand.source: no source; experiments at 0 / moderate / high
demand.note: eta: price sensitivity of customers; lambda: speed at which prices follow costs; spillover: share of unserved demand offered to rivals (0 in the experimental reference).

labor.source: target: S5 for quit and hiring rates, INSEE for unemployment; none checked yet
labor.note: Quarterly quit rate, common probability that a vacancy is filled within the quarter, hiring weights by unemployment duration (re-employment), initial unemployment by pool.

are.source: orders of magnitude; a proxy, not individual rights
are.note: Replacement rate applied to the pool's reference wage, share compensated and amount factor by duration bucket (0–1, 2–4, 5+ quarters).

finance.source: no source; one exogenous ceiling by size, three levels
finance.note: Credit ceiling and cash buffer in months of charges; one interest rate for the overdraft and, later, the investment loan.

planning.source: severance: legal minimum of a quarter of a month per year of seniority, over about five years
planning.note: Planning horizon of the staffing decision, hiring cost per hire and severance per layoff, in months of gross wage.

simulation.source: convention of the spec: 8 quarters after the reform
simulation.note: A burn-in at α = 1, with no investment, is shared by every branch of a seed.

technology.source: no observed price: a grid of costs per A post of capacity, swept
technology.note: One option per firm, sized to the automatable share of its initial A work. Cost, delay, maintenance, transition and lifetime are set independently of wages, and are identical in reference and reform.
